questions.q: The reason for large-scale diversity among the organisms is –
questions.explanation: The group of scientists who gave a modern form to the theory of natural selection is called “Neo-Darwinists”. According to modern Neo-Darwinists, new organisms are formed after small changes in genes, due to which diversity increases in organisms. These changes are called “mutations”. Therefore, the main reason for very high diversity in living organisms is mutation.

questions.q: According to recent proof, the life on earth emerged approximately -
questions.explanation: According to the modern concept, the origin of life on the Earth occurred about 2,000 million (2,000,000,000) years ago. However, the oldest fossils are about 3,600 million years old. Important early fossils are considered to be remains of stromatolites (Stromatolites), which were a group of unicellular organisms. About 2,000 million years ago, eukaryotic cells originated, from which all living organisms of the present living world (except bacteria) were formed.

questions.q: Latest ancestor of modern human is
questions.explanation: Cro-Magnon man anatomically similar to modern humans. He lived in the Stone Age and used bone tools. He had the ability to stitch and wear animal skins. He lived in caves, and his wall paintings are found on cave walls. He is the most recent prehistoric human.

questions.q: The main factor of development is -
questions.explanation: Today, the most accepted theory of evolution is known as the Modern Synthetic Theory of Evolution. In it, the origin (emergence) of species is explained on the basis of interactions of genetic variations and natural selection. In the process of natural selection, the beneficial traits of welladapted organisms are inherited by the next generations, as a result species gradually change over time.

questions.q: The reason for development is -
questions.explanation: The most accepted theory of evolution is the Synthetic Theory of Evolution. In it, the origin of species can be understood on the basis of interactions of genetic variations and natural selection; that is, adaptation from generation to generation is the cause of evolution.

questions.q: Archaeopteryx is –

options.A: The most ancient bird of the Jurassic age
options.B: A reptile of the Jurassic period
options.D: Reptile of both Triassic and Jurassic period

questions.explanation: Archaeopteryx is the oldest bird of the Jurassic age. It is considered a connecting link between birds and reptiles.

questions.q: Which of the following is a warm-blooded animal?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Toad belongs to the class Amphibia, whereas crocodile belongs to Reptilia and fish belongs to Pisces; therefore, none of these three are warm-blooded animals. Hence option (e) is correct.

questions.q: Who was first to use the characteristics of vascular tissues in the classification of plants?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A.P. de Candolle (Augustin Pyramus de Candolle) was a Swiss botanist, who coined the word “taxonomy” for the first time and developed a natural system of plant classification. The systematic use of characteristics of vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) in plant classification was first done by A.P. de Candolle.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of the binomial scientific name?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Under the binomial nomenclature system, the name of a species consists of two parts. The first part is the genus name and the second part is the species name. In the above question, Rana tigrina is the scientific name of a frog. Therefore, it is an example of a binomial scientific name.

questions.q: Protista group includes–
questions.explanation: All unicellular eukaryotic organisms are included in the Protista group. Heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms are included in the Animal Kingdom, and all green plants are included in the Plant Kingdom.

questions.q: In lichen, a chlorophyll-containing partner, __________ live together.

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In lichens, a chlorophyll-containing partner—algae (phycobiont)—and a chlorophyll-lacking partner—fungus (mycobiont)—live together. This is called mutualism. In this type of association, the fungus is the more dominant partner. The fungus provides shelter, water, and minerals to the algae, and in return, the algae provides food to the fungus, which it prepares through photosynthesis. In lichens, reproduction occurs through the fungal component. In biology, when two organisms help each other, it is called a symbiotic (Mutualism) relationship.

questions.q: The interaction between algae and fungi to form lichen is called :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In lichens, a chlorophyll-containing partner—algae (phycobiont)—and a chlorophyll-lacking partner—fungus (mycobiont)—live together. This is called mutualism. In this type of association, the fungus is the more dominant partner. The fungus provides shelter, water, and minerals to the algae, and in return, the algae provides food to the fungus, which it prepares through photosynthesis. In lichens, reproduction occurs through the fungal component. In biology, when two organisms help each other, it is called a symbiotic (Mutualism) relationship.

questions.q: Choose the vascular plant from the following:

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Fern is a non-flowering vascular plant. Vascular plants are those plants in which lignified tissues such as xylem and phloem are present to carry water and minerals from the soil to different parts of the plant.

questions.q: In mycorrhizal association, the advantage of plant is :

options.D: Increased mineral absorption and disease protection

questions.explanation: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association formed between certain fungi and the roots of higher plants. In this association, the plant especially benefits through increased absorption of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other micronutrients. Plants with mycorrhiza also get protection from root-borne diseases and some harmful soil microorganisms.

questions.q: Spirogyra is an example of which of the following algae?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is an example of green algae. It contains chlorophyll; therefore, it makes its own food through photosynthesis. There are more than 400 species of Spirogyra worldwide. Spirogyra is also called water silk.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of algae ?
questions.explanation: Diatoms are unicellular algae. They are organisms found on Earth that have a cell wall made of transparent, opaline silica. They belong to the kingdom Protista.

questions.q: Which of the following is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom?
questions.explanation: Phylum Arthropoda is the largest phylum of the animal kingdom. Among all species found on Earth, nearly twothirds of the species belong to Arthropoda.

questions.q: What is true for phylum echinodermata?

options.A: They are triploblastic and have coelomic cavity.
options.B: They have a peculiar water-driven tube system.
options.C: They are exclusively free living marine animals.
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Phylum Echinodermata: They are exclusively marine organisms. They are multicellular animals with welldeveloped organ systems. Most echinoderms are star-shaped and have a cylindrical body form. They are triploblastic and possess a coelomic cavity. They also have a characteristic water vascular system. They respire through tube feet and dermal bronchiae (skin gills).

questions.q: The animal without red blood cells is –

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Earthworm lacks red blood corpuscles. However, an earthworm appears red because haemoglobin is dissolved in its plasma.

questions.q: The smallest organism, capable of autonomous growth and reproduction, is
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma is the smallest organism that can grow and reproduce autonomously (Self-replicating).

questions.q: Fungi are plants that lack –

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is not found in fungi. For various reasons, fungi are no longer placed in the plant kingdom. Earlier they were included under plants, but fungi are not plants; they belong to a separate kingdom.

questions.q: After bringing out of water fishes die, because-

options.A: They get excess quantity of oxygen
options.D: They can not move in water

questions.explanation: When fish are taken out of water, they die because they cannot breathe. Fish have gills, which are mainly adapted to absorb oxygen (O2) dissolved in water.

questions.q: How do the members of honey-bee hive recognise eachother?
questions.explanation: Almost all animals have methods of exchanging information. They communicate through sight, sound, touch and smell. Honeybees perform different dance patterns to indicate the direction of food and the location of its source, while they recognize each other by smell. These smell-based chemicals are pheromones.

questions.q: Dolphins are classified as –
questions.explanation: Dolphins are aquatic mammals. Many subspecies of dolphins are found; among them, the Ganga river dolphin is India’s National Aquatic Animal.

questions.q: Frogs and toads are examples of which of the following amphibians?
questions.explanation: Frog and toad are examples of amphibians of the order Anura. Major features of Anura include: they have four limbs; their hind limbs are longer and stronger than the forelimbs, which helps them in jumping.

questions.q: Does a bryophyte have a spore mother cell?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In bryophytes, the spore mother cell is diploid. Bryophytes include mosses and liverworts, which are generally found in moist and shady regions of hilly areas. Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom.

questions.q: What is the structural and functional unit of life?
questions.explanation: All living organisms are made up of cells. Some organisms are made of a single cell; they are called unicellular organisms, such as protozoa, Euglena, etc. Organisms like humans, which are made up of many cells, are called multicellular organisms. A unicellular organism can exist independently and perform essential life processes. Anything smaller than a cell cannot ensure independent existence; therefore, the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living beings.

questions.q: The powerhouse of the cell is -

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Mitochondria are double-membrane-bound organelles scattered in the cytoplasm of all living plant and animal cells, except bacteria and blue-green algae (cyanobacteria). They are called the powerhouse of the cell because complete oxidation of glucose takes place in them. Hence, mitochondria are the power source of the cell.

questions.q: Which of the following does not have any enzyme in its cells?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The word “virus” is derived from the Latin word “virus”, which literally means poison or sticky liquid. Viruses are acellular, ultramicroscopic organisms that can multiply only inside a living cell. Generally, enzymes are absent in viruses; however, some viruses such as retroviruses contain certain enzymes. Chemically, a virus is a segment of nucleic acid surrounded by a protein coat. Outside the host cell, viruses can neither perform any biological activity nor replicate. Enzymes are also present in lichen, bacteria, and algae.

questions.q: The substance found in more than 80% of the cell is :
questions.explanation: Water is present in the maximum amount in a cell. Water is the most abundant substance in cells and is about 70% or more of the total cell mass. Therefore, option (d) can be selected as the nearest answer.

questions.q: Which of the following is found both in the cells of a mango plant and a monkey?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the above question, the cell membrane is found in the cells of both the mango plant and the monkey. The cell membrane is semipermeable. It separates the internal part of the cell from the external environment and also provides structural support to the cell.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about permanent tissues is correct?

options.A: They are capable of rapid cell division
options.B: They are found only in young plants
options.C: They lose the ability to divide
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The tissues that are fully developed and have lost the ability to divide are called permanent tissues. Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.q: Plants and animal cells differ in which of the following structure?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cell wall along with a cell membrane. In plants, the cell wall surrounds the cell membrane. It gives a definite shape to the plant cell. Animal cells have a cell membrane, but they do not have a cell wall.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-sense codon?
questions.explanation: In Genetics, a three-nucleotide sequence of mRNA is called a codon. Codons are of two types— Sense codons: These are codons for amino acids and are responsible for protein formation. Their total number is 61. Nonsense (stop) codons: These indicate the termination of protein synthesis. In the standard genetic code, three major stop (nonsense) codons are accepted. These give the termination signal for protein synthesis— UAA (ochre), UAG (amber), and UGA (opal) Therefore, among the given options, only UAA is a nonsense (stop) codon. The remaining are sense codons.

questions.q: Mendel's principle of inheritance is based on-
questions.explanation: Mendel’s theory of heredity is based on sexual reproduction.

questions.q: Which among the following is a character of chloroplast which makes them qualified to self-replication?

options.A: Presence of both DNA and RNA
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The presence of both DNA and RNA is a feature of chloroplasts and mitochondria, which makes them capable of self-replication. It is known that chloroplasts are found in the cytoplasm of all green plant cells. It is a doublemembrane structure.

questions.q: Who discovered DNA?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: It is a misconception that Dr. James Watson, Dr. Francis Crick, M.H.F. Wilkins, and Rosalind Franklin discovered DNA. In fact, on the basis of Wilkins’ X-ray analysis, Watson and Crick presented the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953. Actually, DNA was first identified in 1869 by the Swiss chemist Friedrich Miescher. Friedrich called it “nuclein.”

questions.q: The DNA double helix structure was discovered by :
questions.explanation: It is a misconception that Dr. James Watson, Dr. Francis Crick, M.H.F. Wilkins, and Rosalind Franklin discovered DNA. In fact, on the basis of Wilkins’ X-ray analysis, Watson and Crick presented the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953. Actually, DNA was first identified in 1869 by the Swiss chemist Friedrich Miescher. Friedrich called it “nuclein.”

questions.q: Which of the following is responsible for controlling hereditary characteristics of the living cells?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In living cells, DNA is responsible for controlling hereditary traits. However, the unit of heredity is the gene.

questions.q: Who synthesized the DNA in vitro?
questions.explanation: Arthur Kornberg first synthesized DNA in vitro.

questions.q: Organic farming is an agricultural system in which -

options.A: Chemicals are used to the maximum extent as fertilizers, herbicides and pesticides
options.B: Organic fertilizers, recycled farm wastes and bio-agents are used in minimum quantities
options.C: Organic fertilizers, recycled farm wastes and bio-agents are used in maximum quantities
options.D: Growing two or more crops together in the same field
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In organic farming, the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides is minimum (almost zero), while the use of organic manures, compost manure, agricultural wastes, biofertilizers (such as blue-green algae), etc. is maximum.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct example of organic fertilizer? I. Mycorrhizal fungi II. Blue-green algae III. Bacillus thuringiensis

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Mycorrhizal fungi and blue-green algae (cyanobacteria) are examples of biofertilizers. Bacillus thuringiensis is a bacterium used in Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis) cotton.

questions.q: Advancement occurs through the use of pesticides in terms of:
questions.explanation: By using fertilizers and pesticides, more crops and plants can be produced on less land. They help increase crop productivity. Pesticides also help maximize the benefits of other agricultural inputs such as water resources, fertilizers, and high-quality seeds.

questions.q: The parts of the skeleton that are not as hard as bones and which can be bent are called as

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Cartilage is a type of connective tissue in which there is sufficient space between the cells. Its solid matrix is made of chondrin (protein and sugar). It makes the joints of bones smooth; as a result, friction between bones is reduced. Cartilage is present in the nose, ear, larynx, trachea, and between the bones of the vertebral column. The study of cartilage is called chondrology.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect about muscles in human body?

options.A: Muscles can only push the bone.
options.C: Muscles become shorter, stiffer and thicker when contracted.
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Muscles help a person in activities such as walking, speaking, eating, etc. They assist in heartbeat, respiration, and digestion. Many other functions, including temperature, regulation and vision, also depend on the muscular system. Muscles work in pairs, and on contraction they become shorter, harder, and thicker. Therefore, the statement given in option (a) is incorrect.

questions.q: Muscle contains contractile proteins -
questions.explanation: Contractile proteins are involved in muscle contraction. Actin (thin filament) and myosin (thick filament) are the contractile proteins in muscles.

questions.q: In which organ of the human body is epithelial cells found?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue is a thin and smooth membrane that covers the outer surfaces of all internal organs of the body. Epithelial tissue is found in various organs/parts of the body such as the tongue, kidney tubules, salivary glands, sweat glands, pancreas, lungs, nose, eyes, and ears.

questions.q: Glycogen stored in liver and muscles of the human body is in form of–

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Glycogen stored in the liver and muscles of the human body is a polysaccharide. Polysaccharides are carbohydrates available in abundance in food. When the body does not obtain sufficient energy from food, the body’s energy supply is met by converting stored glycogen into glucose.

questions.q: The number of bones in the hands and feet of an adult human, compared to the total number of bones in a human, is approximately what percentage?
questions.explanation: In an adult human, the total number of bones is 206, whereas the upper and lower limbs (extremities), i.e., the hands and feet, along with the girdles that connect them to the trunk, together have 126 bones; that is, about 60% of the total bones. Their distribution is as follows— (a) Upper (upper extremities) Pectoral (shoulder) girdles → 4 Hands → 60 (b) Lower (lower extremities) Pelvic girdle → 2 Legs → 60

questions.q: How many pairs of nerves arise from the spinal cord?
questions.explanation: 31 pairs of nerves arise from the spinal cord, whereas the number of cranial nerves is 12 pairs.

questions.q: The number of teeth that are developed twice in the lifetime of a human being is –
questions.explanation: In a human’s lifetime, 20 teeth develop twice, and 12 teeth develop only once.

questions.q: The number of bones in the human skull is –
questions.explanation: An adult human skeleton has, on average, 206 bones. The total number of bones in the human skull is 29. Out of these, 8 form the brain case (cranium) around the brain; the remaining include 14 facial bones, 6 middle-ear bones, and one bone called the hyoid bone. It is the only bone in our body that is not attached to any other bone.

questions.q: Leg bone in the human body is –
questions.explanation: In the human body, the leg bone is solid.

questions.q: At the age of 20 years, the number of bones in the human body is approximately-
questions.explanation: The number of bones in the human body at 20 years of age is 206, which is mainly divided into two parts— Axial skeleton (80) Appendicular skeleton (126)

questions.q: Which of the following is not a vestigial organ in humans?
questions.explanation: From morphological and anatomical studies of organisms, we get knowledge about vestigial organs. A vestigial organ appears functionless, but it can be shown to be homologous to an organ that was functional in ancestors. For example, the vermiform appendix in the large intestine of humans, the nictitating membrane of the eye, and the auricular muscles of the pinna. Incisors are not vestigial organs.

questions.q: Which of the following connects a muscle to a bone?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A tendon connects muscle to bone. A tendon helps in the movement of the body’s bones/structures, whereas a ligament connects bone to bone.

questions.q: The type of joint found at the shoulder is also found at the

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the above question, the joint found in the shoulder is also found in the hip.

questions.q: Which one of the following organs most actively functions to regulate our body temperature?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Among the options given in the above question, the skin works most actively to regulate our body temperature.

questions.q: Stapedius is a–
questions.explanation: Stapedius is the smallest muscle in the human body, located in the ears. It helps stabilize the stapes bone. It controls sound and protects the inner ear from damage due to loud noise.

questions.q: In the human system, insulin controls the metabolism of :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Insulin is produced by the pancreas. It is a hormone (a protein) that plays a major role in regulating glucose homeostasis. Insulin also stimulates the process of converting glucose into glycogen in target cells. Glucose is a form of carbohydrate.

questions.q: Energy is stored in liver and muscles in the form of :
questions.explanation: The cells of the body need energy to work. This energy is obtained from the chemical reactions of sugar, fat, and protein. Sugar gets converted into glucose in the body, which is a simple sugar. After absorption, it reaches different organs and tissues through the blood. In the liver and muscles, energy (glucose) is mainly stored in the form of glycogen.

questions.q: Which organ of the human body is affected by typhoid fever?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Disease Affected organ Typhoid (enteric fever), cholera Intestine Tuberculosis, plague, pneumonia Lung Tetanus, leprosy Nervous system Diphtheria, whooping cough Respiratory tract

questions.q: Which of the following human organ is affected by the consumption of aflatoxin food adulterant?
questions.explanation: The liver is a major digestive gland, which gets affected by food poisoning due to aflatoxins. Aflatoxins are toxic substances produced by certain fungi such as some species of Aspergillus and Penicillium, which make food poisonous.

questions.q: The source of the enzyme ‘lipase’ is :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Most lipids in our food are present as simple fats, i.e., triglycerides. The enzyme lipase plays an important role in the digestion of lipids. It breaks lipids into fatty acids and monoglycerides. Lipase is naturally present in the juices secreted by the salivary glands, pancreas, and stomach. Bile has no digestive enzyme, yet it helps in the digestion and absorption of lipids. It emulsifies fats (emulsification). The enzyme pepsin helps in the digestion of proteins.

questions.q: The enzyme which is mixed with food in our mouth is

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Amylase is the main enzyme that mixes with food in the digestive system. Amylase is a type of enzyme or special protein that helps in the digestion of carbohydrates.

questions.q: Which of the following acid is secreted in the stomach ?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is secreted by the parietal/oxyntic cells present in the stomach. It helps in the digestion of food, but if the acid is present in excess in the stomach, indigestion may occur. To get relief from indigestion, we take an antacid such as milk of magnesia, which contains magnesium hydroxide. It neutralizes the effect of excess acid.

questions.q: The sensitive area of the human tongue to bitterness is:

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The front part of the human tongue experiences sweet taste, the back part experiences bitter taste, the side edges experience sour taste, and the front tip and edges experience salty taste.

questions.q: Which gland provides both endocrine and exocrine functions?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The pancreas is a mixed gland, having both exocrine and endocrine types of tissues or cells. The pancreas has two main functions— Exocrine—It mainly helps in the production of enzymes for the digestive system. Endocrine—It mainly regulates blood sugar.

questions.q: Which part of alimentary canal receives bile from the liver ?
questions.explanation: The liver is the largest gland of the human body. It is located just below the diaphragm, connected with the mesentery, and is deep reddish-brown in colour. Its weight is about 1.5 kg. It performs many functions. Some of its main functions are—production of bile, conversion of glucose into glycogen by the process of glycogenesis, etc.

questions.q: Which of the following is not an endocrine gland?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The lacrimal gland (tear gland) is not an endocrine gland. These glands are located above each eyeball, due to which tears are secreted in each eye. They are present in the upper outer (lateral) region of each eyeball. An endocrine gland is a ductless gland, which releases hormones directly into the blood. The organized endocrine glands in our body include the pituitary, pineal, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas, parathyroid, thymus, and the gonads.

questions.q: Which of the following are not the tastes of the tongue? 1. Sweet 2. Bitter 3. Salty 4. Spicy 5. Umami 6. Sour 7. Pungent Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.explanation: Sweet, bitter, salty, sour and umami are tastes of the tongue. Pungent and spicy are not tastes of the tongue. Umami taste is mainly obtained from food items like meat and eggs. Recently, scientists have proposed recognizing ammonium chloride as the sixth taste.

questions.q: Which of the following is mostly carbohydrate?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Among the above options, rice, wheat, barley, maize, etc. are major sources of carbohydrates. However, in 100 grams of cooked rice, the carbohydrate content is about 25.5 grams. In fact, about 90% of the calories in rice come from carbohydrates.

questions.q: The human body contains

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Most of our body is made up of water. In an adult human body, the amount of water is found to be about two-thirds (about 70%).

questions.q: Pellagra is caused by a deficiency of which of the following vitamins?
questions.explanation: Pellagra is a disease caused by deficiency of vitamin B3 (niacin or nicotinic acid). In pellagra, the risk of diarrhea, skin-related disease, and confusion (dementia) increases.

questions.q: The vitamin which is effective in blood clotting is :

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Due to deficiency of vitamin ‘K’ (naphthoquinone), blood clotting becomes slow/delayed. This vitamin is called the antihemorrhagic vitamin. In persons with its deficiency, surgery cannot be performed easily because there remains a risk of excessive blood loss.

questions.q: Which of the following vitamins is used as an antidote to anticoagulant poisons?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Vitamin ‘K’ is used as an antidote for anticoagulant poisons. This vitamin is called the antihemorrhagic vitamin. In persons with its deficiency, surgery cannot be performed easily because there remains a risk of excessive blood loss.

questions.q: In human body, Vitamin A is stored in :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the human body, a considerable amount of vitamin ‘A’ is stored in the liver. The chemical name of vitamin ‘A’ is retinol; its deficiency causes night blindness and xerophthalmia. This vitamin is also called an anti-infective (infection-fighting) vitamin. Its main sources are milk, butter, eggs, fish oil, carrot, etc.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Deficiency of retinol, i.e., vitamin ‘A’, causes xerophthalmia. Deficiency of cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) causes anemia, and deficiency of vitamin ‘D’ (cholecalciferol ‘D3’ and ergocalciferol ‘D2’) causes rickets in children. Beri-beri is caused by deficiency of vitamin ‘B1’ (thiamine), not by deficiency of tocopherol (vitamin ‘E’).

questions.q: Which of the following vitamins is known as Ergocalciferol?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Deficiency of retinol, i.e., vitamin ‘A’, causes xerophthalmia. Deficiency of cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) causes anemia, and deficiency of vitamin ‘D’ (cholecalciferol ‘D3’ and ergocalciferol ‘D2’) causes rickets in children. Beri-beri is caused by deficiency of vitamin ‘B1’ (thiamine), not by deficiency of tocopherol (vitamin ‘E’).

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Sunlight and cod-liver oil are rich sources of Vitamin D. Wheat-germ oil is a major source of Vitamin E, while alfalfa contains Vitamin K in large amounts. Although orange is a major source of Vitamin C, it also contains Vitamin B1 in a very small amount. Therefore, option (e) is the correct answer.

questions.q: Which of the following vitamins contain Cobalt –
questions.explanation: Cobalt is a mineral salt, which is an important component of Vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin/cobalamin). Vitamin B12 is essential for growth, and its deficiency can also disturb the physiology of the nervous system. Important sources of Vitamin B12 are meat, fish, liver, milk, cheese, etc. Intestinal bacteria also synthesize it.

questions.q: Cobalamin is the scientific name of which of the following vitamins?
questions.explanation: Cobalt is a mineral salt, which is an important component of Vitamin B12 (cyanocobalamin/cobalamin). Vitamin B12 is essential for growth, and its deficiency can also disturb the physiology of the nervous system. Important sources of Vitamin B12 are meat, fish, liver, milk, cheese, etc. Intestinal bacteria also synthesize it.

questions.q: Insulin is :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above.

questions.explanation: Insulin is an animal hormone secreted by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the endocrine part of the pancreas. From the viewpoint of chemical structure, it is a small peptide (protein) composed of 51 amino acids. It regulates glucose metabolism in the body and converts glucose into glycogen.

questions.q: Substances which are responsible for catalyzing chemical reactions in living systems are -
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts. They are generally proteins and, like other catalysts, increase the rate of reaction. options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Thyroxine, an iodine-containing hormone, is an amino acid, and it is secreted by the thyroid gland. questions.q: Which of the following is the best source of vitamin A?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Among the given options, carrot is the best source of Vitamin A. questions.q: Which of the following vitamins are water soluble ?
questions.explanation: The Polish scientist Casimir Funk first proposed the concept of vitamins and was the first to use the term “vitamin”. So far, about 13 types of vitamins are known, which are mainly classified into two categories— (i) Water-soluble vitamins: Vitamins B complex and C (ii) Fat-soluble vitamins: Vitamins A, D, E and K Vitamins are also called accessory food factors.

questions.q: Yeast is used in the production of _____.

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Yeast, mainly Saccharomyces cerevisiae, is used for the production of alcoholic beverages like alcohol and beer because it converts the sugar of grains into ethanol. It is also used in the production of bread. It is also used as a nutritional supplement for humans.

questions.q: Which of the following activities increases oxygen in the carbon cycle occurring on Earth?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the process of photosynthesis, water and carbon dioxide are used and oxygen is released. Therefore, in the carbon cycle on Earth, photosynthesis increases oxygen.

questions.q: During expiration the diaphragm becomes

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The process in which fresh air from the atmosphere reaches our lungs and impure air comes out of the lungs is called breathing (Breathing). This process is completed in two parts— (i) Inhalation (Inspiration), (ii) Exhalation (Expiration). In exhalation (Expiration), carbon dioxide (CO2)-rich air comes out of the lungs. In this, the ribs and diaphragm return to their normal position. The volume of the lungs decreases again. As a result, pressure on the lungs increases and carbon dioxide rich air is expelled from the body. During exhalation, the diaphragm is pulled upward and becomes dome-shaped.

questions.q: During normal respiration in mammals, the diaphragm is-

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In mammals, during inhalation (inspiration) the diaphragm becomes flattened. In fact, the diaphragm located below the lungs and spreading the thoracic and abdominal cavity is a respiratory muscle in mammals, which helps in the process of breathing.

questions.q: A clinical death takes place when

options.C: Pupils are fixed and dilated and there is no reaction to light
options.D: All the above three conditions are present together
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Clinical death is not actual death; it means , a person can be revived by CPR or other measures. Clinical death is declared when the following conditions are present together— → Pulse has stopped → Heartbeat has stopped → The pupils are fixed and dilated and show no reaction to light.

questions.q: In how many steps CO2 is released in aerobic respiration?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: During aerobic respiration, carbon dioxide (CO2) is released in three different stages. These stages are as follows— At the time of formation of Acetyl CoA (Acetyl-Coenzyme A), During the Krebs cycle during the conversion of isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutaric acid, and During the Krebs cycle during the conversion of alpha ketoglutarate arale to (Succinyl-CoA).

questions.q: The most important cell type associated with the immunity of the body is

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Lymphocyte is the most important cell type related to the body’s immunity because it is the WBC that secretes the maximum amount of antibody proteins. Lymphocytes are formed in the bone marrow and are found in blood and lymphatic tissues. Lymphocytes are mainly of two types— B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes. Notably, in response to pathogens, B-lymphocytes produce a chain of proteins in human blood so that they can fight pathogens. These proteins are called antibodies (Antibodies). T-lymphocytes do not secrete antibodies themselves, but they help Blymphocytes in producing these proteins (antibodies). These are important parts of the immune system, which protect the body from diseases caused by pathogens.

questions.q: Leukemia is a name for several types of cancer that originate in the bone marrow and cause a large number of abnormal blood cells to form. Which blood cell is this?
questions.explanation: Leukaemia is a group of blood-related cancers that originate in the bone marrow. In this condition, the number of white blood cells (WBCs) in the blood increases abnormally. WBCs are very important for the body’s immune system, as they protect the body from infections. In leukaemia, the abnormal white blood cells formed are not fully developed, and by crowding out normal blood cell formation, they weaken the body’s immune system.

questions.q: Which one of the following is used in the treatment of blood cancer?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Radio-phosphorus (P-32) and cobalt-60 are used in the treatment of leukaemia (a type of blood cancer).

questions.q: The total volume of blood in a normal adult human being is
questions.explanation: Blood is a liquid connective tissue. It continuously circulates inside blood vessels through different organs. In humans, the amount of blood is about 7 to 8 percent of body weight. Therefore, in a healthy adult of about 70 kg body weight, there are approximately 5 to 6 litres of blood, which is about one-thirteenth of the total body weight.

questions.q: The function of hemoglobin is -

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Haemoglobin carries oxygen from the lungs to the body tissues and carries carbon dioxide back to the lungs. That is, the function of haemoglobin is to transport oxygen. Oxygen is required for blood circulation and for the functioning of all body organs, in which haemoglobin plays an important role.

questions.q: What prevents backflow of blood during heart contraction?

options.B: Thick muscular walls of the ventricles

questions.explanation: During heart contraction, the heart valves prevent the backflow of blood. The atria store blood and their walls are thin. The ventricles pump blood to different parts of the body. Since blood pressure is higher in the ventricles, their walls are thick.

questions.q: In transfusion, blood must be compatible not only in blood type, but also in -

options.D: race of the donor and recipient
options.E: none of the above / more than one of the above

questions.explanation: In blood transfusion, along with the blood group, the Rh factor must also be compatible. The Rh factor was discovered by Landsteiner and Wiener in the blood of the rhesus monkey.

questions.q: Which of the following instrument measures blood pressure –
questions.explanation: A normal human blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg. There are two stages of blood pressure in arteries. The first is called systolic pressure and the second is called diastolic pressure. Generally, systolic pressure is 120 mmHg and diastolic pressure is 80 mmHg. Doctors measure blood pressure using a sphygmomanometer.

questions.q: In which organ of the human body are the lymphocytes formed?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the human body, lymphocytes are produced in the spleen, thymus gland, bone marrow, etc. Lymphocytes are a type of white blood cells (WBCs). They move throughout the body like a patrolling force and establish coordination among all parts of the immune system.

questions.q: Which among the following help in circulation of blood?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Erythrocytes (red blood corpuscles) generally help in the transport of oxygen in blood. Their main function is to carry oxygen from the lungs to all body tissues and to help in transporting apart of carbon dioxide back to the lungs.

questions.q: Blood group of an individual is determined by
questions.explanation: According to Mendel’s laws, a person’s blood group is determined on the basis of genes inherited from the parents. Its inheritance depends on genes/alleles of three (rather than two) contrasting characters.

questions.q: The universal acceptor blood group is :

options.E: None of the above / more than one of the above

questions.explanation: A person with group O (O–) can donate blood to all groups; therefore, it is called the universal donor. It is worth noting that a person with AB group can receive blood of any group, but their blood cannot be given to a person of another blood group. Hence, a person with AB (AB+) is called the universal recipient.

questions.q: The blood group of universal donor is –
questions.explanation: A person with group O (O–) can donate blood to all groups; therefore, it is called the universal donor. It is worth noting that a person with AB group can receive blood of any group, but their blood cannot be given to a person of another blood group. Hence, a person with AB (AB+) is called the universal recipient.

questions.q: Myoglobin contains the metal –
questions.explanation: Myoglobin is an iron containing and oxygen-binding protein found in the muscles of vertebrates, whereas haemoglobin is found in blood (in red blood cells).

questions.q: The process of blood purification in the human body is called -
questions.explanation: The artificial process of blood purification in the human body is called dialysis.

questions.q: Which of the following is the fluid part of the blood ?
questions.explanation: Human blood is a fluid connective tissue. It supplies oxygen and nutrients to body tissues and carries CO2 and other waste products away from them. Blood has four components—plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Plasma constitutes about 55% of blood and the remaining components about 45%. Plasma contains mostly water (around 92%).

questions.q: Defective hemoglobin in the blood is seen in which of the following?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Sickle cell anemia is a genetic disorder. Due to this, red blood cells become sickle-shaped. It affects hemoglobin, which is a major protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen. Normally, red blood cells are biconcave and flow easily through blood vessels. This disease affects the hemoglobin molecule, changes the shape of red blood cells, and makes them sickle (crescent shaped) which can obstruct blood flow.

questions.q: Lacteals are associated with which of the following?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Lacteals are lymph vessels present in the villi of the small intestine. They are similar to blood capillaries, but their diameter is larger than that of blood capillaries. Their main function is to absorb fats present in the digested food in the small intestine.

questions.q: The most important cell type associated with the body's immune system is -

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Lymphocyte is the smallest white blood cell (WBC). Its main function is to destroy disease-causing organisms through immune responses and thereby increase the body’s immunity. Among all WBCs, it secretes the maximum amount of antibodies.

questions.q: In Tachycardia, the heart rate becomes

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Tachycardia is a medical term related to heart rate. When the heart beats 100 times or more in one minute, it is called tachycardia in medical science. In this condition, the heart rate becomes faster than normal. If the heart beats less than 60 times per minute, it is called bradycardia.

questions.q: The average blood flow through kidneys per minute is –
questions.explanation: The kidney is an important organ of the human body. Its main function is to purify the blood and remove toxic substances from the body through urine. Human kidneys filter about 180 liters of blood daily and produce about 1.5 liters of urine. About 1200 c.c. of blood flows through the kidneys per minute, which is nearly 1/5 of the blood pumped out by the heart in one minute.

questions.q: Which one among the following glands is present in pair in human body?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the human body, the adrenal gland is present in pairs. It is an endocrine gland found in vertebrates. It is located above the kidneys. Its function is to produce hormones that control important processes inside our body.

questions.q: The filtration unit in human kidney is called as a

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The filtration unit in the human kidney is called the nephron. It is used to separate water, ions, and small molecules from blood, filter wastes and toxic substances, and send necessary molecules back into the blood.

questions.q: In humans, the kidneys are part of which system?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In humans, the kidneys are a part of the excretion system. The kidneys filter liquid waste from the blood and form urine.

questions.q: Electroencephalogram (EEG) is used to monitor which of the following?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The control center of reflex actions is the spinal cord. The spinal cord is a cylindrical structure. Through it, we receive stimuli, and based on their nature, reflex actions are mainly of two types— (1) Unconditioned and (2) Conditioned. Due to reflex action, when the foot steps on a thorn, we immediately pull the foot backward.

questions.q: Which of the following organs in the body controls the body's balance?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Macula and crista ampullaris present inside the ear maintain body balance. In addition, the cerebellum, also called the small brain, is a part of the hindbrain. It is also responsible for maintaining body balance and posture.

questions.q: Input and output nerves meet at :
questions.explanation: Afferent (Sensory) and efferent (Motor) nerve impulses originated from the central nervous system. The central nervous system (CNS) is the processing center of the nervous system. The CNS includes the brain and spinal cord. The major functions of the CNS are processing information, controlling blood pressure and respiration, and regulating and coordinating body functions, etc. The CNS works like the central processing unit (CPU) of the body.

questions.q: Which of the following glands is called the 'third eye' of the human body?
questions.explanation: The Pineal gland is a very small gland located in the human brain, is called the “third eye” of the human body. It is the smallest endocrine gland in the human body. questions.q: Which of the following is an enhancement of the innate system?
questions.explanation: The autonomic system is a part of the peripheral nervous system. It controls involuntary functions. Therefore, the development of the autonomic system can be defined as the self-regulatory activity.

questions.q: The female sex hormone is :

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Estrogen is a hormone produced in females by the cells of the theca interna of Graafian follicles in the ovary, from puberty up to the age of menopause (about 45 to 55 years). The main estrogen is estradiol, which is called the female development hormone because it helps in the development of secondary sexual characters (including proper development of breasts, mammary glands, uterus, vagina, etc.) in females.

questions.q: Which of the following rays/waves is used to know the development of the fetus in the womb?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: To know the development of the fetus in the womb, ultrasonic waves are used in ultrasonography.

questions.q: Sexual reproduction causes genetic variation because of -
questions.explanation: Genetic variation occurs through sexual reproduction due to gene blending, changes in chromosomes, and gene shuffling—all three.

questions.q: Where does fertilization occur?
questions.explanation: In humans, fertilization is internal. Through sexual intercourse, the male gamete (sperm) enters the female reproductive tract. Sperm are highly active and motile. Millions of sperm enter the vagina and move towards the uterus through the cervix. Finally, only one sperm fertilizes the ovum in the oviduct (fallopian tube).

questions.explanation: In the chloroplast, solar energy is converted into ATP. The chloroplast is a plant cell organelle in which a proteincontaining complex chemical compound called chlorophyll is found. This pigment is responsible for the green colour of leaves.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true for the breathing process?

options.B: Energy is released and stored as ATP
options.C: Energy is released and stored as ADP.
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In the process of respiration, energy is released and stored in the form of ATP. In living cells, the process by which energy is produced as a result of oxidation of food is called cellular respiration. During this process, the released energy is stored in the biomolecule ATP.

questions.q: Plants appear to bend towards light due to–

options.A: Concentration of auxins at shoot tip
options.B: Concentration of auxins at root tip
options.C: Diffusion of auxins towards the shady side of the shoot
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Auxins are synthesized at the tip of the shoot and help cells to elongate for a longer time. When light falls on the plant from one side, auxin diffuses towards the shaded side of the shoot. The higher auxin concentration on the shaded side stimulates the cells there to elongate more (i.e., on the side away from light). Therefore, the plant appears to bend towards the light.

questions.q: Water passes from the soil into the root by the physical process is called -

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Water reaches the roots from the soil through the process of osmosis.

questions.q: Photosynthesis occurs—

options.C: During the day or at night

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is a process in green plants in which they prepare food. In this process, light provides the energy. Naturally, plants obtain energy from sunlight, but marine algae can perform this process in moonlight, and photosynthesis can also occur in plants under electric light.

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is a process in green plants in which they prepare food. In this process, light provides the energy. questions.q: Where does photosynthesis take place in the cells of a leaf?
questions.explanation: The process of photosynthesis occurs in all chloroplastcontaining cells of the plant, i.e., in all green parts of the plant. This process occurs especially in the mesophyll tissue of leaves.

questions.q: Which of the following the chlorophyll in photosynthesis is used for ?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants, in the presence of sunlight, form carbohydrates by the combination of water and carbon dioxide. In this process, oxygen is released as a by-product. Chlorophyll is a chemical photoreceptor (light-absorbing pigment) that captures light for photosynthesis in plants. It absorbs light mainly in the red (long wavelength) and blue (short wavelength) regions of the visible spectrum. Absorption of green light is very low, and the green light is reflected. That is why a plant appears green.

questions.q: Chlorophyll absorbs ______ wavelengths of the sunlight.

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is a photoreceptor (light-sensitive) chemical that absorbs light for photosynthesis in plants. It absorbs visible light mainly in the red (long-wavelength) and blue (short-wavelength) regions. Absorption of green light is very low, and green light is reflected. That is why plants appear green.

questions.q: The process of breaking down organic matter by micro organisms is called :
questions.explanation: Decomposers are those biotic components that, for their nutrition, decompose the dead bodies (organic matter) of producers and consumers. These mainly include microorganisms (especially bacteria and fungi). As a result of this process, complex organic substances are decomposed into simpler organic substance such as carbon dioxide, water and mineral nutrients (e.g. nitrate, phosphates, calciumetc.

questions.q: Which of the following is a plant hormone?

options.E: None of the above
