questions.q: Which of the following plants has modified its stem to store food material?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Plants such as turmeric, ginger, and potato store food material in modified stems, whereas radish, carrot, beetroot, turnip, sweet potato, etc. are modifications of roots.

questions.q: Water is conducted in vascular plants by-
questions.explanation: Water and mineral nutrients absorbed by roots are carried throughout the plant by the conducting tissue called xylem, whereas phloem transports food.

questions.q: Which pigment is essential for nitrogen fixation by leguminous plants?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Leghemoglobin is an important pigment for nitrogen fixation in leguminous plants. It protects the nitrogen-fixation enzyme system from oxygen, which is harmful to it.

questions.q: The most important part of the plant in terms of its life cycle is–
questions.explanation: From the life-cycle point of view, the flower is the most important part of the plant. In the flower, the embryo develops through pollination, which forms the seed. On germination of the seed, a new plant is formed again.

questions.q: Pea plant is :
questions.explanation: Pea is a dicotyledonous herbaceous plant. It is a rabi crop. Swarna Rekha, Aparna, Paras, Ambika, etc. are its main varieties.

questions.q: Legumes are highly nutritious because they are rich in:

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Pulses contain a large amount of protein. Their plants belong to the family Leguminosae/Fabaceae. Their root nodules contain bacteria that fix nitrogen. Examples—pea, pigeon pea (arhar), green gram (moong), soybean, groundnut, black gram (urad), etc.

questions.q: Xylem in plants is responsible for following function:

options.B: Transport of water and dissolved minerals
options.C: Transport of oxygen and other gases

questions.explanation: Xylem is one of the vascular (conducting) tissues of vascular plants. Its main function is to carry the water and dissolved mineral salts absorbed by the roots to the stem, leaves, and other parts of the plant. This transport generally occurs from bottom to top (from root to leaf), so it is considered unidirectional transport.

questions.q: The stomata open or close due to changes in the

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: During the day, due to higher transpiration, water is absorbed by the roots and transported to different parts of the plant through xylem, due to which the guard cells become swollen (turgid). As a result, the stomata open. At night, the guard cells shrink and become rigid because the roots absorb less water; therefore, the stomata close. Potassium plays an important role in the opening and closing of stomata.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a correct match?

options.B: Thick, hard stem with branching near the base: Tree
options.C: Weak stem which cannot stand upright: Creeper
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: A plant with a thick, hard stem and branches near the base is not a tree; it is a shrub. Note that plants play the role of major producers on Earth. Also, plants are known by different names in different forms: the petiole connects the leaf to the stem, and a creeper (vine) is a type of weak stem that cannot stand upright without support.

questions.q: The stem of the plant helps in distributing food to all parts of the plant. It also helps in -

options.E: None of the above / more than one of the above

questions.explanation: The stem helps in distributing food (nutrients) along with water to all parts of the plant and also in storing food (nutrients). It supports the leaves, flowers, and fruits and plays a major role in giving shape to the plant as well.

questions.q: Water reaches great heights in trees because of suction pull caused by

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Transpiration is a process in which loss of water vapour occurs through the stomata of (mainly leaves). The loss of water vapour from the plant cools the plant when the weather is very hot.

questions.q: The part which we eat in Mango is :
questions.explanation: From a botanical point of view, mango is a single-seeded fleshy fruit (Drupe). In such fruits, the pericarp is divided into three parts— 1. Exocarp/Epicarp – the peel of the mango. 2. Mesocarp – the fleshy pulp that we eat. 3. Endocarp – the inner hard layer, seen as the hard stone in mango.

questions.q: The edible part of litchi is -

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Litchi is a tasty, juicy subtropical fruit. The edible part of litchi is the aril. Botanically, litchi belongs to the family Sapindaceae. In India, the highest production of litchi is in Bihar.

questions.q: Ginger is a stem, not a root, because-

options.C: It grows horizontally in the soil.
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Ginger (botanical name: Zingiber officinale) is a modified underground stem, not a root, because it has nodes and internodes. It is a rhizome, i.e., an underground modification of the stem. A rhizome is a branched, prostrate, horizontally growing stem. Other examples of rhizomes are turmeric, banana, and fern.

questions.q: Ginger is an underground stem and not a root because

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Ginger (botanical name: Zingiber officinale) is a modified underground stem, not a root, because it has nodes and internodes. It is a rhizome, i.e., an underground modification of the stem. A rhizome is a branched, prostrate, horizontally growing stem. Other examples of rhizomes are turmeric, banana, and fern.

questions.q: Water enters from soil into root hairs of plants due to

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In plants, the basic process of water absorption occurs through root hairs. These root hairs remain in contact with soil particles, and the cells absorb water due to osmotic pressure. Each root hair has a vacuole filled with cell sap.

questions.q: What is the movement of the leaves of the sensitive plant Mimosa pudica called?
questions.explanation: The movement of leaves of the sensitive plant Mimosa pudica is called seismonasty (a response to touch/shock). It is a feature found in some plants, in which responce occurs when the plant is touched or shaken in any way.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a vegetative hormone?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Cytokinin is a plant hormone. Plant hormones control the development, growth, and reproductive processes of plants. Insulin is an animal hormone (a peptide/protein hormone). Estrogen is a group of hormones that plays an important role in normal sexual and reproductive development in women.

questions.q: Plants are formed like parent plant from –
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation is an asexual method of reproduction. In this method, new plants are obtained from parts of old plants (such as stem, root, and leaves) without the involvement of reproductive organs. Stem cutting, layering, and grafting are common methods. New plants produced by asexual reproduction are morphologically and genetically similar to their parent. In contrast, plants produced by sexual reproduction (from seeds) show variations.

questions.q: Embryo is found in –
questions.explanation: In plants, the embryo is found in the seed. As a result of the germination process, the embryo comes out of the seed.

questions.q: Water-pollinated flowers have pollen grains that are:

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In water-pollinated flowers, pollen grains are dry.

questions.q: Stem cutting is done generally to grow –
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation of sugarcane is done by stem cuttings (called setts) or by ratooning. However, with each ratoon crop, the yield keeps decreasing after every 3–4 years, fresh stem cuttings with buds have to be replanted.

questions.q: Among the following, which is not a true fruit?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: If, in the formation of a fruit, some parts other than the ovary are also involved, such a fruit is called a false fruit. Examples— apple, cashew nut, pear, pineapple, strawberry, etc.

questions.q: Buds are specifically found—

options.A: At the base (axil) of leaves and at the ends of branches

questions.explanation: Buds are specifically found in the axils of leaves and at the ends of branches (at both ends, as stated). The development of buds on leaves indicates the process of growth and maturity in plants.

questions.q: The part of the flower that gives rise to a fruit is

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A flower is the reproductive organ of a plant. In a flower, calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium are present. The androecium is the male reproductive part, while the gynoecium is the female reproductive part. In the gynoecium, the pistil is present, which has three parts— ovary, style and stigma. Later, the ovary of the flower develops and takes the form of a fruit.

questions.q: Pollination is best defined as –

options.A: transfer of pollen grains from anther to stigma
options.C: growth of pollen tube in ovule
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In scientific terms, pollination is the process in which pollen grains are transferred from anther to the stigma. After fertilization, the ovary develops into a fruit and the ovules develops into seeds.

questions.q: A plant bud is –
questions.explanation: In botany, an undeveloped shoot (embryonic shoot) is called a bud or budlet. It arises either in the axil of a leaf or at the terminal end of the stem.

questions.q: Clove, a spice, is obtained from which part of the plant?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Cloves are dried flower buds, used in food items, as a pain reliever, etc. The botanical name of clove is Syzygium aromaticum, which belongs to the family Myrtaceae. Indonesia is considered its place of origin, and it is used throughout the world. It is an evergreen tree, about 10–20 meters tall, and its leaves are large and oval.

questions.q: Cloves are obtained from which of the following parts of the plant?
questions.explanation: Cloves are dried flower buds, used in food items, as a pain reliever, etc. The botanical name of clove is Syzygium aromaticum, which belongs to the family Myrtaceae. Indonesia is considered its place of origin, and it is used throughout the world. It is an evergreen tree, about 10–20 meters tall, and its leaves are large and oval.

questions.q: Turmeric powder is obtained from which part of the turmeric plant ?
questions.explanation: Turmeric powder is obtained from the underground stem of the turmeric plant, i.e., the rhizome. After cutting the rhizome and removing the outer layer, the remaining part is dried and ground to make turmeric powder.

questions.q: What is the scientific name of the spice 'Curcuma longa'?
questions.explanation: ‘Curcuma longa’ is the scientific name of turmeric. The scientific name of cumin is Cuminum cyminum, the scientific name of clove is Syzygium aromaticum, and the scientific name of coriander is Coriandrum sativum.

questions.q: Pine, Fir, Spruce, Cedar, Larch and Cypress are the famous timber-yielding plants of which several also occur widely in the hilly regions of India. All these belong to –

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Pine, fir, spruce, cedar, larch and cypress are well-known timber-yielding plants. They are coniferous trees found in mountain forests. All of these are gymnosperms.

questions.q: Insulin is received from -
questions.explanation: Inulin is a polysaccharide. It is found in the roots of dahlia, onion, garlic, banana, and shatavari (Asparagus).

questions.q: Quinine is a common drug for malaria that is obtained from a plant. Which part of the plant yields this drug?
questions.explanation: Quinine is an important medicine for the treatment of malaria. It is obtained from the bark of the Cinchona plant. This plant is an angiospermic. Quinine is a natural white crystalline alkaloid with a bitter taste. It is also used in the treatment of nocturnal leg cramps.

questions.q: Where does aspirin come from?
questions.explanation: Aspirin and antipyretic (fever-reducing) medicines act as pain relievers. They are obtained from the bark of the willow tree.

questions.q: Aspirin is -
questions.explanation: Aspirin is an antipyretic.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not an antibiotic?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Oxytocin is a hormone found in mammals. It is produced in a part of the brain called the hypothalamus and is secreted by the pituitary gland. It has a special role in bonding and social attachment ; therefore, it is also called the “love hormone”, whereas erythromycin and penicillin, etc. are examples of antibiotics.

questions.q: Which one of the following is an antibiotic drug?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Chloramphenicol is an antibiotic medicine used for the treatment of bacterial infections. Sulfaguanidine is a type of sulfonamide antibiotic, which works as an antibacterial agent. Thus, more than one option is correct for this question.

questions.q: Which of the following is an antibiotic?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Among the above options, penicillin and sulfadiazine are antibiotics. Antibiotics are used for the treatment of diseases caused by bacteria. Therefore, the correct answer is option (e).

questions.q: An example of an antibiotic drug is -

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Among the above options, penicillin and sulfadiazine are antibiotics. Antibiotics are used for the treatment of diseases caused by bacteria. Therefore, the correct answer is option (e).

questions.q: The longest living tree is-
questions.explanation: The tallest/highest tree is the coastal redwood (Sequoia sempervirens) or Hyperion, whose height, according to Guinness World Records, is about 116.07 metres.

questions.q: Which of the food grains is richest in protein?
questions.explanation: Among plant foods, soybean has the maximum protein content. Its protein content is approximately 38–42%, which is higher than other pulses.

questions.q: The largest flower in the world is-
questions.explanation: The world’s largest flower is Rafflesia arnoldii. It was first discovered by Joseph Arnold in 1818. The weight of this flower can be up to about 7-11 kg.

questions.q: Match List–I with List–II : List-I List-II (Cloth) (Origin) A. Linen 1. Coconut plant B. Coir 2. Flax plant C. Mohair 3. Feathers of ducks and geese D. Down 4. Angora goat Select the correct answer using the codes given below. A B C D
questions.explanation: The correct matching is as follows— Cloth Origin Linen Flax plant Coir Coconut plant Mohair Angora goat Down Feathers of ducks and geese

questions.q: Which one of the following term characterizes the interaction between herpes simplex virus and a human?
questions.explanation: A parasite requires the host cell’s metabolic energy and the host’s protein-synthesis system for replication, and this causes harm to the host cell. Therefore, such a biological relationship is called parasitism. The Herpes simplex virus lives inside human cells and is completely dependent on them for nutrition and replication, and it harms humans; hence, the “interaction” (biological relationship) between the two is correctly termed parasitism, which is expressed by option (a). Endoparasitism is also essentially a subtype of parasitism in which the parasite lives inside the host’s body. This is also applicable in the context of the interaction between Herpes simplex virus and humans. Possibly considering this as correct, the Bihar Public Service Commission gave its answer as option (d).

questions.q: AIDS is caused by :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: AIDS is a viral disease. AIDS is caused by HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus).

questions.q: The disease caused by HIV is –
questions.explanation: AIDS is a viral disease. AIDS is caused by HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus).

questions.q: The Ishihara test is related with
questions.explanation: Ishihara test is a method used to test for colour blindness. This test was developed by the Japanese scientist Dr. Shinobu Ishihara.

questions.q: Pneumonia is an infection of -

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Pneumonia is an infection of the lungs, which causes inflammation in one or both lungs. This infection can be caused by viruses, bacteria, fungi, etc.

questions.q: The most common carrier of communicable diseases is

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The most common carrier of infectious diseases is the house fly, because it carries germs from dirty places and contaminates human food. Also, by landing on human body parts, it helps in the spread of infectious diseases.

questions.q: Name a clinical trial in which blood is transfused from a recovered COVID-19 patient to a coronavirus patient who is in critical condition.
questions.explanation: Through plasma therapy, plasma from a recovered COVID-19 patient is transfused into a coronavirus patient in serious condition. It is noteworthy that this method is used to transfer protective antibodies present in the plasma to help the patient fight the infection.

questions.q: How do COVID vaccines stimulate an immune response?

options.A: By introducing live attenuated SARS-CoV-2 virus
options.B: By introducing a real SARS-CoV-2 virus
options.C: By introducing a harmless piece of SARS-CoV-2 virus
options.D: By introducing antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 virus

questions.explanation: COVID vaccines stimulate the immune response by introducing a harmless part of the SARS-CoV-2 virus (such as the spike protein) or instructions to make it, so the body produces antibodies and develops immune memory.

questions.q: How do vector vaccines work to provide immunity?

options.A: By introducing a weakened or inactivated virus into the body
options.B: By directly attacking and destroying pathogens in the body
options.C: By placing the virus in a modified version of a different virus
options.D: By entering directly into the cells and enabling them to create spike proteins

questions.explanation: Vector vaccines work to provide immunity by using a modified version of another virus to deliver the required genetic material into the body. This enables the body to produce the target antigen and develop an immune response.

questions.q: Which of the following bacterial disease that is called as splenic fever ?
questions.explanation: Splenic fever is caused by the bacterium Bacillus anthracis, which causes anthrax. Anthrax is a disease that occurs due to contact with infected animals.

questions.q: The incubation period of hepatitis B virus is

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: After some time following infection, symptoms of diseases appear. This period is called the incubation period. The incubation period of the Hepatitis B virus is about 75 days, but it can range from 30 to 180 days. Hepatitis B is an infectious disease caused by a virus and spreads through blood. Hepatitis B is the most common liver infection in the worldwide. It is caused by the Hepatitis B virus.

questions.q: Typhoid and cholera are typical examples of –
questions.explanation: Typhoid and cholera are examples of waterborne diseases. Typhoid is caused by Salmonella typhi and cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae. They can be prevented from spreading by proper treatment and Purification of drinking water.

questions.q: BCG vaccine is used for the prevention of :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: BCG (Bacillus Calmette–Guérin) vaccine should be given immediately after a baby’s birth for protection against tuberculosis (TB). If it has not been given immediately after birth, it can be given within 12 months of birth, but as more time passes after birth, its protective effect may decrease.

questions.q: Biodegradable waste can usually be converted into useful substances with the help of:'

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Biodegradable waste is generally converted into useful substances by bacteria.

questions.q: Every year 5 lakhs of Indians die of a disease. Identify it-
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis (Yakshma/Tapedik/Kshaya Rog) is an infectious disease caused by a bacterium named Mycobacterium tuberculosis. In this disease, the human lungs are affected. Symptoms include fever, continuous cough, blood in the sputum, shortness of breath, etc. According to the Global TB Report 2025 released by the World Health Organization in November 2025, India has recorded a 21% reduction in the annually reported new TB cases. In 2015, the number of TBaffected persons per lakh population in India was 237, which decreased to 187 in 2024. This is almost double the global rate of decline (12%).

questions.q: Decomposers of dead organisms are-

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Microorganisms that decompose dead plants and animals are called decomposers. Both bacteria and fungi come under decomposers.

questions.q: Besides spreading Malaria, Anopheles mosquitoes are also vectors of
questions.explanation: Apart from spreading malaria, Anopheles mosquitoes are also carriers of the diseases encephalitis and filariasis.

questions.q: Female Anopheles can be distinguished from female Culex because it sits

options.A: At right angle to the surface of the substratum
options.B: At an angle with the substratum
options.C: Parallel to the surface of the substratum
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Female Anopheles can be distinguished from female Culex because it rests at an angle to the substratum. Globally, more than 3,500 species of mosquitoes are found, and they are divided into three genera—Culex, Anopheles, and Aedes. Each genus works as an intermediate host for a specific parasite. Besides this, there are sufficient differences among them in terms of food chain, shape, habitat, etc. Difference between Culex and Anopheles– Culex Their eggs are laid in clusters on the surface of water. Their larvae feed from below. Their wings are transparent. They are capable of flying long distances. Their body remains parallel to the substratum. Anopheles Eggs are laid separately (not in clusters) on the water surface. They lay eggs in a horizontal pattern. Their larvae feed from above. Their wings are spotted. They cannot fly long distances. Their body rests at an angle to the substratum.

questions.q: Which statement regarding malaria is not true?

options.A: It is a disease caused by an insect parasite.
options.C: It occurs mostly in marshy areas.
options.D: Chloroquine is used in its treatment.

questions.explanation: The causative organism of malaria is a protozoan named Plasmodium, which is a digenetic organism, and its carrier (vector) is the female Anopheles mosquito. Malaria is more common in marshy areas, and chloroquine is used for its treatment. It is stated to be obtained from the bark of a plant called Cinchona.

questions.q: Store house of malarial parasite in our body is–

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Malaria is a disease caused by Plasmodium parasites. It spreads through the bite of an infected Anopheles mosquito and has remained a major threat to global health throughout history. Among the five species of Plasmodium that infect humans, Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax pose the greatest health risk to populations in malariaendemic regions. Therefore, both the liver and the spleen are affected.

questions.q: Which mosquito bite causes malaria?
questions.explanation: Malaria fever is an infectious disease spread by mosquitoes, which occurs due to the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito. This female mosquito contains a special type of protozoan parasite, which in medical language is known as Plasmodium.

questions.q: Consider the following statements : 1. Taeniasis is an intestinal infection caused by three species of tapeworm—Taenia solium, Taenia saginata and Taenia asiatica. 2. When cysts develop in the brain, the condition is referred to as neurocysticercosis (NCC). Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Taeniasis is an intestinal infection caused by three species of tapeworm—Taenia solium, Taenia saginata, and Taenia asiatica. Some symptoms of taeniasis are diarrhea, increased appetite, or loss of appetite, etc. Neurocysticercosis (NCC) is a parasitic disease of the brain, caused by Taenia solium or the pork tapeworm. In this disease, cysts develop in the brain. Therefore, both statements 1 and 2 are correct.

chapters.chapter_name: V. Deficiency, Non-Contagious and Other Disease

questions.q: What happens due to iron deficiency in the body?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Deficiency of iron in the body causes anemia. Iron is essential for the formation of hemoglobin in the blood. Inadequate intake of iron-rich food leads to iron deficiency in the body.

questions.q: Oncogenes are associated with –
questions.explanation: It was first identified as V-Src. The first oncogene identified was V-Src, discovered in the 1970s in the Rous sarcoma virus, a cancer-causing virus of chickens.

questions.q: Which of the following can cause cancer as well as cure it depending upon its intensity and use?
questions.explanation: Ionizing radiation is the factor that can cause cancer and is also used in its treatment. In radiation therapy, ionizing radiation is used to destroy cancer cells and shrink tumors. Research has made it clear that even low and moderate radiation exposure can cause cancer, and prolonged exposure radiation can also cause cancer.

questions.q: In respect of women, men can suffer more of colour blindness because-

options.A: They pass more through mental tensions
options.B: They live out of home relatively more

questions.explanation: Compared to women, men suffer more from colour blindness because women have two (XX) sex chromosomes. If one X carries the gene for colour blindness, the other normal X chromosome compensates for it. Thus, the woman generally acts only as a carrier and is not affected, whereas the man becomes affected.

questions.q: The active chemical in mosquito-repellent products is—
questions.explanation: The compound called allethrin is the active chemical in mosquito-repellent products.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: BCG vaccine is given to prevent tuberculosis. Artemisin, Chloroquine, etc., are used to treat malaria. Scurvy is a disease caused by Vitamin C deficiency, while Thiamine is known as Vitamin B1.

questions.q: Trachoma disease is related to-

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Trachoma is related to the eye. Trachoma is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis. Due to infection, the inner surface of the eyelids becomes rough. This roughness can cause eye pain, damage to the cornea, and ultimately blindness.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs are correctly matched? 1. Anorexia : Sleep disorder 2. Insomnia : Eating disorder 3. Dyspnoea : Shortness of breath 4. Anosmia : Partial or full loss of smell Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.explanation: Anorexia — Anorexia nervosa is an eating-related disorder. A person suffering from it remains anxious/apprehensive about body weight, due to which they avoid eating food. Insomnia — Insomnia is a sleep disorder. A person suffering from it faces problems such as difficulty in falling asleep, walking up too early or having disturbed sleep and not getting good-quality sleep etc. Dyspnea — Dyspnea (dyspnoea) is a disorder related to breathing problems. Anosmia — It is a disorder related to the sense of smell. A person suffering from it has difficulty in smelling. Since pairs 3 and 4 are correctly matched, the required answer option (a) is correct.

questions.q: To diagnose the medical conditions, MRI technique is used. Which is not used in MRI?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a medical imaging technique. To obtain images of body organs through MRI, a strong magnetic field and radio waves are used. It is also called Magnetic Resonance Tomography (MRT). Both Xrays and gamma rays are high-frequency ionizing radiation, meaning they have sufficient energy to remove electrons from an atom or molecule. In both ultrasound and MRI, no ionizing radiation is used.

questions.q: Who was the first scientist/doctor, who attempted vaccination?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Edward Jenner first began vaccination in 1796.

questions.q: The name of the gas used to artificially ripen raw fruits is-
questions.explanation: Both acetylene and ethylene gases are used for fruit ripening. However, at present, the use of acetylene for artificial fruit ripening is not permitted. Naturally, fruits ripen due to the ethylene hormone. Ethylene gas is also being used for artificial ripening.

questions.q: Har Gobind Khorana is credited for the discovery of –
questions.explanation: Har Gobind Khorana was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1968 jointly with Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg “for their interpretation of the genetic code and its function in protein synthesis”.

questions.q: Animal clones are created by the practice of ____.'

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Biotechnology is a technology based on biology. Biotechnology uses cellular and biomolecular processes to develop technologies and products that help improve our lives and the health of the Earth. Animal clones are produced using biotechnology.

questions.q: The process of determining the relative positions of genes on a chromosome is called -

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The process of finding the relative positions of genes on a chromosome is called gene mapping. It is used to determine gene order and to calculate the distance between genes.

questions.q: What is the expanded form of the term ‘mRNA’ that has been widely discussed since the beginning of the pandemic?
questions.explanation: The expanded form of mRNA is Messenger Ribonucleic acid. Messenger RNA is a type of single-stranded RNA that is involved in protein synthesis. mRNA-based vaccines were developed to prevent COVID-19.
